transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Occupational health sent me over. They’re saying my weight is dangerously low, especially for the kind of work I do running presses and fabrication all day. I guess I didn’t see it that way—I thought I was just getting leaner, more disciplined.
Have you been intentionally restricting your food intake?

Yes. Most days I keep it pretty limited. I’ll have coffee before the early shift, maybe half a protein bar at lunch, and then after yoga I might eat a small bowl of vegetables. Eating more than that just makes me feel like the whole day is out of control.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. If the scale goes up even a little, I panic. It feels like I’m going to lose all the control I’ve worked so hard for and end up heavy again.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t really have times where I eat a lot and can’t stop. It’s usually the opposite—I’m trying to keep it small.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?
Not really. I don’t usually feel out of control while I’m eating… I feel more anxious about eating too much, so I try to keep it controlled.
How much weight have you lost over the past few months?

I’m not exactly sure of the number… but enough that occupational health sent me here. They said my weight is dangerously low for the kind of work I do running presses and fabrication all day. I thought I was just getting leaner, honestly… more disciplined.
Have you ever had an episode where you ate an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period?
No, I can’t think of a time like that. I don’t really eat big amounts at once… if anything, I’m usually watching it pretty closely.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that is much larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time, even if it was something you planned?
No, I don’t think so. Even if I plan what I’m going to eat, it’s usually not a lot. I can’t remember eating a really large amount in a short time like that.
Do you regularly engage in excessive exercise, such as your yoga, as a means to burn off calories or prevent weight gain?

I’m not sure I’d call it excessive. I do yoga sometimes, but I don’t really think of it as “burning off” food. It’s more just… something I do. I haven’t really noticed it being about calories, at least not in a clear way.
Is your yoga routine something you feel you need to do to maintain your current weight?

I guess… yes, in a way. It’s less about the yoga itself and more that if the scale goes up even a little, I panic. I feel like I’m going to lose control and end up heavy again, so I do feel like I have to stay on top of it.
Have you ever had times where you felt like you were eating in secret because you were ashamed of how much you were eating?

I don’t think so. I mean, I might eat alone sometimes, but not because I’m hiding a large amount of food or anything like that. I haven’t really had times where I felt ashamed because of how much I was eating.
Have you ever felt like you were going to throw up after eating because you felt like you had eaten too much?
I don’t think so. I might feel uncomfortable or anxious after eating sometimes, but not like I’m actually going to throw up because I ate too much.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
No… I don’t make myself throw up after eating.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating a normal or small amount of food?
I’m not sure I’d call it losing control. Even with a small amount, I can feel uneasy about eating it, but it’s not like I suddenly can’t stop or don’t know what I’m doing.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to lose weight or prevent weight gain?
No, I don’t use laxatives or water pills for that.
Do you avoid eating in front of other people because you're worried about what they might think of your eating habits?
I don’t know… I guess I haven’t really paid attention to that specifically. I don’t think it’s mainly about what people think, at least not that I could say for sure.
Is your decision to limit your food intake mostly driven by a fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?
Yes. I mean… that’s a big part of it. If the scale goes up even a little, I panic. It feels like I’m going to lose all the control I’ve worked for and end up heavy again.
Have you ever had times where you felt like you were eating an amount of food that was much larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had times like that, at least not where it was clearly a much larger amount than other people would eat. I mostly just worry about eating too much, even when it probably isn’t that much.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt like you were eating in a way that was not controlled, even if you didn't eat a large amount of food?

I’m not sure. I mean, I worry I’m not in control if I eat more than I planned, but I can’t really say I’ve had an episode like that where it felt out of control. It’s more that I get anxious about it afterward.
Have you ever had times where you felt like you were eating in a way that was not controlled?
I don’t think so. Like I said, I get upset if I eat more than I meant to, but I wouldn’t say I’m eating in a way where I can’t control myself. It’s more the worry afterward.
